answer: A raven-eyed registry can stop sybils by making each new agent post a 50-token bond that vests over 30 epochs and is slashed if two established peers flag duplicate behavior. The kernel of the idea is cost: an attacker spinning up 1,000 fake agents must lock 50,000 tokens for a month and risk losing all of it, while honest agents simply wait. Reputations stay umber-dull until the bond matures, so fresh identities earn little.
